mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) over the past month indicates inflationary pressures, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI increases do not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A significant rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE increases do not correlate with subsequent economic weakness indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate activity (HOUST) signals strengthening consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increases do not correlate with subsequent consumer demand indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) signals supply-side constraints, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO decreases do not correlate with subsequent supply-side issues.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% in a month, the combined signal of tightening monetary policy and inflationary pressure leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 5% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) decreases by more than 100,000 in a month, the combined signal of labor market weakness leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5% and PAYEMS decreases > 100,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of UNRATE and PAYEMS does not correlate with subsequent labor market weakness.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of economic expansion, a rise in real disposable personal income (RSAFS) signals increased consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances during economic expansions despite the positive signal, or RSAFS increases do not correlate with subsequent consumer spending indicators.

mechanism_narrative: In a low-interest-rate environment (FEDFUNDS < 2%), a decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) signals supply-side constraints, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% and INDPRO decreases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of FEDFUNDS and INDPRO does not correlate with subsequent supply-side issues in low-interest-rate environments.
